subject: pelican spider
title: This Spider Impales Other Spiders and Holds Them at Fang's Length

scenes.text: This spider hunts other spiders and keeps them at fang's length.
It's a pelican spider from Madagascar, as long as a grain of rice.
Its fanged jaws stick out on a long neck, like a pelican's beak.
It plucks other spiders' webs to lure them out.
Then it stabs, lifts the victim into the air, and lets the venom work.
Dangling, the victim likely can't fight back. Fossils show this design is a hundred sixty-five million years old.

description:
Pelican spiders hunt other spiders and hold them at fang's length.
Found only in Madagascar, these rice-grain-sized hunters have long, neck-like bodies and beak-like jaws. They lure or track other spiders, stab them with fang-tipped jaws and hold them in the air while the venom works, likely to avoid a counterattack. Living species look like fossils up to 165 million years old.
Would you keep one as a pet to clear out other spiders?
first_comment: In 2018 one scientist described 18 new pelican spider species at once, and she thinks more are still out there. Which would scare you more, the spider or its prey?
